2023_082_m121322bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held December 13, 2022 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, with President Schmidt presiding and Mr. Gottlieb absent. The Board awarded the BP 9952 2023 Site Work retention pond bid to Simone Construction Services for $421,901.00 from the Building and Site Sinking Fund and approved an Agreement of Purchase and Sale preserving 69.51 +/- acres of Section 1 with Six Rivers Land Conservancy. The principal action was Resolution 22-089 authorizing the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) in an amount not to exceed $190,000,000, the first series under the $555,000,000 proposal approved by electors on November 8, 2022.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, December 13, 2022, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:0X p.m. Present with him were Board members Anne, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson; Mr. Gottlieb was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, and West, with approximately 35 members of the audience. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Recognition and Public Comment**
The Student Spotlight honored a Troy High School sophomore in the Creative Guild who had recently wrapped up editing on her directorial debut short film; Thomas Butcher, Creative Content Producer from the TSD Creative Guild, shared a clip. There were no additions or deletions. Mr. Jeff Schaeper, Troy resident, addressed the Board about the District budget and future deficit and offered his assistance.

**Consent Agenda (22-086)**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mrs. Hammond; items A through E approved.

| Item | Content |
| --- | --- |
| A | Minutes of the November 1, 2022 Board of Education Workshop |
| B | Minutes of the November 15, 2022 Board of Education Meeting |
| C | Treasurer's Report — October 2022 |
| D | IA Letter of Understanding |
| E | General Fund Budget Amendment #1 |

Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb. No personnel or curriculum items were presented.

**Business Actions**
Each carried on the same roll call: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

| Res. | Subject | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 22-087 | BP 9952 2023 Site Work – Retention Pond Project | Bid awarded to Simone Construction Services, $421,901.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund. Moved Hammond, supported Anne. |
| 22-088 | Purchase Agreement – Section 1 Preservation | Authorized sale and preservation of the remaining 69.51 +/- acres of Section 1 to Six Rivers Land Conservancy, a Michigan non-profit corporation, following the March 20, 2018 resolution splitting Section 1; Superintendent or designee authorized to execute. Moved Philippart, supported Anne. |
| 22-089 | 2023 School Building and Site Bond Sale Authorizing Resolution (Series 1) | Authorized issuance of the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $190,000,000. Moved Hauff, supported Anne. |

**Bond Resolution Highlights**
The bonds are the first series under the 2022 Bond Proposal approved by electors at the General School Election of November 8, 2022, authorizing issuance in one or more series not to exceed $555,000,000. Parameters: denominations of $5,000 or integral multiples; maturities on May 1 or November 1 with final maturity not later than thirty years from the date of issue; true interest cost not exceeding 6.50% per annum; underwriter's discount not exceeding 0.50% of principal. Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated was appointed senior managing underwriter; Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. as bond counsel; PFM Financial Advisors LLC as municipal advisor. Tax levies begin with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2023. Exhibits cover the bond form and a continuing disclosure undertaking under SEC Rule 15c2-12, with annual filings to the MSRB through EMMA commencing with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023.

**Public Communication — Non-Agenda**
Speakers were Mrs. Katie MacFarland (MASB correspondence about a Maryland court case related to gender support), Mrs. Barb Yagley (Covid precautions and funding; recommended The Real Anthony Fauci), Mr. Edmund Rushton of Plymouth (field trips to the Museum of African History in Detroit), and Mr. Ollie Apahidean (pursuit of truth in teaching; Code of Conduct violations).

**Other**
Student representatives Yara Mashal (International Academy-East) and Sara Ali (Athens High School) reported; Nish Palepu (Troy High School) and Alexi Papadelis (Troy College and Career High School) were absent. Members thanked Mrs. Hammond for her years of service. Dr. Machesky praised the fine arts teachers and the SSAB Executive Board's MLK Day event, for which fleece donations are needed. Mr. Schmidt announced a Board Workshop on January 10, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting on Tuesday, January 17th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. Adjourned at 7:55 p.m.
2023_082_m121322bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, held December 13, 2022 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:0X p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Anne, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson; Mr. Gottlieb was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, and West. Approximately 35 members of the audience attended. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION — STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The Student Spotlight celebrated the talents and achievements of students in the Creative Guild. The Board recognized a sophomore from Troy High School who had recently wrapped up editing on her directorial debut short film. Thomas Butcher, Creative Content Producer from the TSD Creative Guild, was invited up to share a clip and talk about the work that went into the student project from start to finish.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS. None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS). Mr. Jeff Schaeper, Troy resident, addressed the Board about the District budget and future deficit and offered his assistance.

GENERAL — CONSENT AGENDA, RESOLUTION 22-086. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Hammond that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D and E on the consent agenda: Minutes of the November 1, 2022 Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the November 15, 2022 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report — October 2022; IA Letter of Understanding; and General Fund Budget Amendment #1. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

PERSONNEL. None. CURRICULUM. None.

BUSINESS — BP 9952 2023 SITE WORK / RETENTION POND PROJECT, RESOLUTION 22-087. It was moved by Mrs. Hammond and supported by Mrs. Anne that the bid for site work projects be awarded to Simone Construction Services in the amount of $421,901.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

BUSINESS — PURCHASE AGREEMENT, SECTION 1 PRESERVATION, RESOLUTION 22-088. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne. The recitals note that on March 20, 2018 the Board passed a resolution that the School District property commonly known as Section 1 should be split into two parcels, so the front portion could be sold to a developer for residential purposes and the remaining portion would be preserved in perpetuity. The School District negotiated an Agreement of Purchase and Sale for the sale and preservation of the remaining 69.51 +/- acres of Section 1 with Six Rivers Land Conservancy, a Michigan non-profit corporation, whose mission is to conserve, sustain, and connect natural areas, lands, and waters that make the places we live special. The Agreement, already executed by Six Rivers, is attached as Exhibit A. The resolution authorizes the sale and preservation of the Premises on terms substantially similar to the attached Agreement and authorizes the Superintendent, or his designee, to execute it, any extensions, and all other incidental documents. Certified by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, as duly adopted at a regular meeting held on the 13th day of December, 2022, in full compliance with the Open Meeting Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

BUSINESS — 2023 SCHOOL BUILDING AND SITE BOND SALE AUTHORIZING RESOLUTION (SERIES 1), RESOLUTION 22-089. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Board authorize the issuance of bonds designated the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $190,000,000, and that the attached resolution in its entirety be made part of the official minutes of the December 13, 2022 regular meeting.

The attached resolution, captioned TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT, COUNTY OF OAKLAND, State of MICHIGAN, RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (UNLIMITED TAX GENERAL OBLIGATION), records a regular Board meeting held in the School District on December 13, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. local time. The preamble and resolution were offered by Member Gary Hauff and supported by Member Vital Anne.

Recitals: at the General School Election held November 8, 2022, qualified electors approved the issuance of bonds, in one or more series, in an amount not to exceed $555,000,000 (the 2022 Bond Proposal), for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting and completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom additions and other additions to existing school buildings and other facilities; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; acquiring sites, preparing, developing and improving sites; and the purchase of school buses. Under Section 6, Article IX and Section 16, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, tax levies for the bonds are without limitation as to rate or amount. The Board authorized the first series in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $190,000,000. The Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually, are designated the Authorized Officer. The School District must either be granted qualified status under Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, or receive prior approval from the Michigan Department of Treasury.

Bond details: registered as to principal and interest in the denomination of $5,000 or integral multiples; dated as of the date of delivery or another date set by the Authorized Officer; maturing on May 1 or November 1, with final maturity not later than thirty (30) years from the date of issue; interest at rates determined upon negotiated sale not exceeding a true interest cost of six and one-half percent (6.50%) per annum, payable semi-annually on May 1 and November 1; underwriter's discount not to exceed 0.50% of principal. Interest is payable by check drawn on the Transfer Agent to the registered owner of record as of the fifteenth day of the month prior to each payment date. Bonds may be issued in book-entry-only form through The Depository Trust Company in New York, New York, as serial or term bonds, subject to optional or mandatory redemption as determined by the Authorized Officer.

Funds: the Treasurer shall open a special depositary account designated the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Debt Retirement Fund, unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund is established, and an account designated the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Projects Fund (the Capital Projects Fund). Net original issue premium counts against the 2022 Bond Proposal. Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2023, the School District must levy a tax annually sufficient to pay principal and interest, without limitation as to rate or amount. Arbitrage rebate obligations arise under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

Sale and professionals: the Board determined that a negotiated sale provides greater flexibility in structuring maturities and timing. Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated was appointed senior managing underwriter, with authority for the Authorized Officer to appoint co-managing underwriters and to negotiate, award, execute and deliver a bond purchase agreement without further Board approval. Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. was appointed bond counsel, with disclosure of Miller Canfield's periodic representation of Stifel in unrelated matters; PFM Financial Advisors LLC was appointed municipal advisor. The Authorized Officer may apply for bond ratings and municipal bond insurance, approve preliminary and final official statements, exercise authority under Section 315(1)(d) of the Act, apply to Treasury for prior approval or file a qualifying statement, request rating waivers, file a Security Report, and pursue qualification under the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005, as amended. Continuing disclosure is covenanted under SEC Rule 15c2-12. Vote on the bond resolution: YES 6, NO 0, ABSENT Gottlieb; declared adopted and certified by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, citing the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of 1976, as amended.

EXHIBIT A — BOND FORM. The form of the Troy School District 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) provides interest computed on the basis of a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months, payable semiannually, with principal payable at the corporate trust office of the Transfer Agent, changeable on not less than 60 days' notice. The bonds are issued under Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, as amended, and Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, pursuant to the resolution adopted December 13, 2022, and constitute the first series authorized by the majority vote of qualified electors at the November 8, 2022 General School Election. The full faith and credit of the School District is irrevocably pledged. Redemption notice must be given at least 30 days and not more than 60 days prior to the redemption date; bonds are called in multiples of $5,000, and redemption is at par plus accrued interest. The Transfer Agent need not register transfers during the 15 days before the mailing of a redemption notice.

EXHIBIT B — FORM OF CONTINUING DISCLOSURE UNDERTAKING. Defined terms include Audited Financial Statements (prepared by independent certified public accountants as required by Act 2, Public Acts of Michigan, 1968, as amended), Bondholders, EMMA (the MSRB's Electronic Municipal Market Access system), Financial Obligation, MSRB, the Rule (SEC Rule 15c2-12 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934), and SEC. The School District agrees to provide to the MSRB through EMMA, on or before the last day of the 6th month after the end of its fiscal year, commencing with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023, annual financial information and operating data similar to Official Statement tables covering: ENROLLMENT — Historical Enrollment; STATE AID PAYMENTS; PROPERTY VALUATIONS — History of Valuations; MAJOR TAXPAYERS; SCHOOL DISTRICT TAX RATES (per $1,000 of Valuation); TAX LEVIES AND COLLECTIONS; RETIREMENT PLAN — Contribution to MPSERS; DEBT STATEMENT — DIRECT DEBT; SCHOOL LOAN REVOLVING FUND (SLRF) PROGRAM; and GENERAL FUND BUDGET SUMMARY in Appendix C, plus the Audited Financial Statements (unaudited statements filed if audited ones are unavailable). The undertaking requires notice of failure to disclose and, within ten business days, notice of sixteen listed events including payment delinquencies, unscheduled draws on debt service reserves or credit enhancements, adverse tax opinions and IRS notices such as Form 5701-TEB, bond calls and tender offers, defeasances, rating changes, bankruptcy or receivership, mergers or asset sales, and defaults under a Financial Obligation. Further provisions address materiality under federal securities laws, termination of the reporting obligation upon legal defeasance, enforcement limited to specific performance for the benefit of Bondholders, and amendment procedures consistent with the Rule.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mrs. Katie MacFarland, Troy resident and parent of students in the District, addressed the Board about emails exchanged between MASB and Board members regarding a court case from Maryland related to gender support. Mrs. Barb Yagley, Troy resident, addressed the Board regarding Covid, precautions to keep children safe, and Covid funding, and recommended reading the book The Real Anthony Fauci. Mr. Edmund Rushton, Plymouth resident, addressed the Board about offering field trips to visit the Museum of African History in Detroit, located near the DIA, to learn about racism and history. Mr. Ollie Apahidean, parent of students in the District, addressed the Board about teachers teaching children how to pursue the truth and asked about the Code of Conduct and violations.

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES. Yara Mashal (International Academy-East) and Sara Ali (Athens High School) shared reports on events and activities at their schools. Nish Palepu (Troy High School) and Alexi Papadelis (Troy College and Career High School) were not in attendance.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS AND ADJOURNMENT. Board members wished everyone happy holidays; Mrs. Hammond shared a heartfelt goodbye and members thanked her for her years of service to the board and community. Dr. Machesky congratulated the fine arts teachers for the numerous holiday concerts, gave a shout out to the SSAB Executive Board for bringing back the District's annual MLK Day event, and noted that donations of fleece are desperately needed, along with a blood drive and other community activities. Mr. Schmidt announced a Board Workshop on January 10, 2023 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting on Tuesday, January 17th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. The meeting adjourned at 7:55 p.m.
